dossier_meta.statement_text: For every natural number $m$, does there exist a natural number $n$ such that $E^n \not\to (\ell_3, \ell_m)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: In the concluding remarks the authors say they were unable to decide this question. They consider it unlikely to hold for large $m$ but were unable to exhibit a coloring confirming their suspicion. Erdős et al. [3] showed that $E^n \to (\ell_6, \ell_6)$ for all $n$, providing related context.
